sections.html:
Start by choosing between an agent, a private sale and a cash buyer. Whichever you pick, Boone County's tax and recording offices handle the back end: the county assesses, bills and records, and the city deals with permits and rental rules.

Florence belongs to Boone County and the Cincinnati metro area. No other Kentucky city that lacks a county seat is bigger. Census takers found 31,946 people in 2020, and the 2025 estimate stands at 34,018, a 6.4% rise. Of all homes, 57.5% have their owners living in them. House values in the middle of the market are $210,700, rent is $1,329 and household income is $71,003. The 2020 count listed 13,003 households among 13,624 housing units, with 4.6% vacant. Only 1.2% of owner homes sat empty.

U.S. 25, 42 and 127 run through the center and reach downtown Cincinnati, about 12 miles northeast. Interstates 71 and 75 cross the western side, with exits 178 through 182. St. Elizabeth Healthcare, Boone County Schools, Robert Bosch, Walmart, Costco and the city itself employ people inside the city, and Turfway Park racetrack lies within its limits.

sections.h2: What goes on a Boone County tax bill
sections.html:
Every Boone County bill carries seven lines: the state, the county, the schools, the extension district, the library, the Northern Kentucky Health Department and a fire district. Florence owners also pay a city property tax, plus a flat $75 a year for each occupied dwelling to fund the 911 system, a fee that began in 2018.

Bills reach owners each October. Two things set the amount: the assessed value from the state's PVA office and the rate each taxing entity sets. The Fiscal Court sets only the county's share. Read the payment dates printed on your own bill, or ask the Boone County Sheriff. Keep a copy of the paid bill in your sale folder, since buyers and title agents will ask for it. After April 15, unpaid bills sit with the county clerk carrying a 10% penalty, a sheriff's add-on fee and interest of 1% for each month.

sections.h2: How to challenge an assessment before selling
sections.html:
It is possible, but the window is short. This is the order Kentucky follows.

  • Anyone can view the tax roll for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May.
  • Sit down with the PVA or a deputy. Without that conference, no appeal can be filed.
  • Take the appeal to the county clerk by the end of the first working day after inspection closes.
  • The local assessment appeals board hears it 25 to 35 days later. Bring sales listings, building costs, insurance policies and a property description, because a case with no evidence is denied.
  • If you file and then skip the hearing, the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

Homeowners past 65, and owners with a total disability, can ask the PVA for a homestead reduction. It takes $49,100 off the assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The break stays with the person, so a buyer applies on their own after closing. If you qualify and have not yet filed, call the PVA before you list, since the lower bill helps your carrying costs while the house is on the market. Proof of age or disability is what the office will want to see.

If your house has hosted overnight guests, the city permit does not go to the buyer. Florence treats any stay under 30 consecutive days as a short-term rental, wants one permit for each property, and issues it only to the named applicant at that address.

  • The fee is $500 and the host needs $1,000,000 in liability coverage.
  • Most residential zones allow the use only as a conditional use, and the Boone County Planning Commission issues that permit before the city acts.
  • Conditional-use rentals must be 1,000 feet apart, a rule that does not apply in the Main Street Overlay District.
  • Guests are capped at two per bedroom plus two, and concerts or weddings are banned.

The city lists 859-647-5413 for rental questions. Buyers who want the same use must start their own application.

sections.h2: What a Florence sale costs the seller
sections.html:
Deed tax under KRS 142.050 comes to $0.50 per $500 block of value and is paid to the clerk when the deed goes into the county record. Other costs usually dwarf it: your mortgage payoff, repairs, and your slice of this year's property tax. Get a payoff letter and the current bill before comparing offers.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before accepting an offer
sections.html:
Organized paperwork shortens the stretch from signed offer to deed.

  • The latest Boone County bill, showing the city line and the $75 911 fee.
  • A lender payoff letter dated close to the planned closing day.
  • Any short-term rental permit, inspection form or insurance certificate.
  • Leases and deposit records when tenants live in the house.
  • Receipts and permits for roof, furnace and addition work done since you bought.

Give the closing agent these items on day one, and ask the Boone County Sheriff whether any earlier year remains open. A cash sale can close fast on a house that needs work, provided title is clear and tax bills are paid out of the proceeds.

Renters fill a large share of Florence homes. When a tenant occupies yours, work out early whether the buyer keeps the lease or expects a vacant unit. Leases generally outlast a sale, which passes the rent and deposit to the new owner unless your contract says differently. Give the buyer's side the lease and deposit records along with the tax bill, and nobody is caught off guard later. Tell the tenant about the sale in writing, and ask the closing agent how the deposit should be credited.

A cash purchase means no underwriting queue, and no appraisal can shave the price after you shook hands. The buyer accepts the property as it stands, aging roof and half-built addition included. County steps still apply: the deed is recorded, deed tax is due and unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds. Request a net figure in writing at the start, then set it beside what a listing would likely leave you after commissions and repairs.

faqs.q: Do Florence owners pay city property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone inside an incorporated city like Florence owes a city tax in addition to the county's seven bill lines, and your own bill shows each amount.

faqs.q: What is the Boone County 911 fee?
faqs.a: A flat $75 a year for each occupied dwelling, whatever its assessed value. It began in 2018 and appears on the property tax bill.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over my Florence short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. The permit belongs to the applicant at that address and cannot move to anyone else. A new owner applies fresh, and most residential zones also call for a conditional use permit.

faqs.q: By when must a Boone County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: By the close of the first working day after inspection ends, once you have met with the PVA. The roll opens the first Monday in May for 13 days, and you file with the county clerk.

faqs.q: How much deed tax would a Florence seller owe?
faqs.a: Half a dollar for each $500 block of value on the deed, paid by the seller to the clerk at recording.
